    - article:
      - heading "Unraveling the role of gravity in shaping intruder dynamics within vibrated granular media" [level=3]:
        - link "Unraveling the role of gravity in shaping intruder dynamics within vibrated granular media":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01927-9
      - paragraph: Granular segregation may play a role in shaping the surface features of small celestial bodies such as asteroids that can be explained with the Brazil-nut effect. The authors study intruder dynamics in granular media on board the Chinese Space Station, finding that contrary to what occurs on Earth intruders tend to descend in microgravity conditions under specific vibration parameters
      - list:
        - listitem: Ke Cheng
        - listitem: ", Meiying Hou"
        - listitem: ... Mingcheng Yang
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 30 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "One-third magnetization plateau in Quantum Kagome antiferromagnet" [level=3]:
        - link "One-third magnetization plateau in Quantum Kagome antiferromagnet":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01922-0
      - paragraph:
        - text: A range of non-trivial quantum phenomena can emerge from frustrated magnetic systems and a prime example is a quantum spin liquid. Here, the authors conduct specific heat and magnetization measurements on the Kapellasite-type compound InCu
        - subscript: "3"
        - text: (OH)
        - subscript: "6"
        - text: Cl
        - subscript: "3"
        - text: in order to characterize and define the range of the magnetization plateau in this material.
      - list:
        - listitem: Moyu Kato
        - listitem: ", Yasuo Narumi"
        - listitem: ... Hiroyuki K. Yoshida
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 28 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Two-dimensional cooling without repump laser beams through ion motional heating" [level=3]:
        - link "Two-dimensional cooling without repump laser beams through ion motional heating":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01920-2
      - paragraph:
        - text: Reducing the number of lasers in laser cooling experiments is beneficial for simplifying systems requiring multiple repumping frequencies. This work demonstrates micromotion-assisted cooling of Be
        - superscript: +
        - text: ions with a single laser, eliminating the need for a 1.25 GHz offset repump laser, with results rigorously validated through molecular dynamics simulations.
      - list:
        - listitem: Yue Xiao
        - listitem: ", Yongxu Peng"
        - listitem: ... Tiangang Yang
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 27 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "DarkSide-20k sensitivity to light dark matter particles" [level=3]:
        - link "DarkSide-20k sensitivity to light dark matter particles":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01896-z
      - paragraph: The DarkSide-20k collaboration reports the sensitivity of its detector, currently under construction, to models predicting light dark matter particles. This includes Weakly Interacting Massive Particles and particles interacting with bound electrons of argon atoms.
      - list:
        - listitem: F. Acerbi
        - listitem: ", P. Adhikari"
        - listitem: ... M. P. Zykova
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 26 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Distorted insights from human mobility data" [level=3]:
        - link "Distorted insights from human mobility data":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01909-x
      - paragraph: Human mobility data is crucial for many applications, but researchers often rely on single datasets assuming universal validity. Comparing 7 diverse sources across 145 countries, we find significant differences in mobility patterns and networks, impacting applications like epidemic modeling and emphasizing the need for transparent data processing.
      - list:
        - listitem: Riccardo Gallotti
        - listitem: ", Davide Maniscalco"
        - listitem: ... Manlio De Domenico
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 24 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Electronic cooling via acoustic-enabled low-power compact heat exchanger" [level=3]:
        - link "Electronic cooling via acoustic-enabled low-power compact heat exchanger":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01915-z
      - paragraph: Improving the cooling performance of high-power electronics in confined spaces remains a challenge. Herein, the authors propose an acoustic-enabled low-power compact heat exchanger that utilizes contactless acoustics as a flexible active means for enhancing phase change cooling.
      - list:
        - listitem: Junsheng Hou
        - listitem: ", Dongyu Li"
        - listitem: ... Nanjing Hao
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 23 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Quantum origin of anomalous Floquet phases in cavity-QED materials" [level=3]:
        - link "Quantum origin of anomalous Floquet phases in cavity-QED materials":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01908-y
      - paragraph: Non-equilibrium systems subject to periodic driving fields, known as Floquet materials, can host unique topological phases without static counterpart. This work targets the link between Floquet physics and cavity-QED systems, and unveils the emergence of quantum anomalous phases in the latter, pointing to the important entangled light-matter dynamics.
      - list:
        - listitem: Beatriz Pérez-González
        - listitem: ", Gloria Platero"
        - listitem: "& Álvaro Gómez-León"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 21 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Channel-resolved wavefunctions of transverse magnetic focusing" [level=3]:
        - link "Channel-resolved wavefunctions of transverse magnetic focusing":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01902-4
      - paragraph: Transverse magnetic focusing (TMF) has been widely used in mesoscopic physics, yet its quantum mechanical properties remain difficult to fully appreciate. Here, the authors present a numerical solution of TMF, analysed with channel-resolution and compared against experimental data, to expose the multichannel signatures of the TMF wavefunction.
      - list:
        - listitem: Seokyeong Lee
        - listitem: ", Dongsung T. Park"
        - listitem: ... Hyung Kook Choi
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 20 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "High-energy tunable ultraviolet pulses generated by optical leaky wave in filamentation" [level=3]:
        - link "High-energy tunable ultraviolet pulses generated by optical leaky wave in filamentation":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01910-4
      - paragraph: High-energy ultraviolet pulses serve as unique light sources for strong-field physics and ultrafast science. The authors theoretically demonstrate the generation of ultraviolet pulses with sub-mJ level energy via optical leaky wave in filamentation, where preformed gasplasma channels are used to provide adjustable dispersion conditions that enable a widely tunable wavelength range of the ultraviolet pulses.
      - list:
        - listitem: Litong Xu
        - listitem: "& Tingting Xi"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 20 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Direct visualization of local magnetic domain dynamics in a 2D Van der Walls material/ferromagnet interface" [level=3]:
        - link "Direct visualization of local magnetic domain dynamics in a 2D Van der Walls material/ferromagnet interface":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01861-w
      - paragraph: This study explores how the interface between Permalloy and graphene affects the propagation of magnetic domains. Using advanced transmission electron microscopy and simulations, the research reveals key insights that could advance future memory and logic technologies.
      - list:
        - listitem: Joseph Vimal Vas
        - listitem: ", Rohit Medwal"
        - listitem: ... Rajdeep Singh Rawat
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 19 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Development of a Helmholtz free energy equation of state for fluid and solid phases via artificial neural networks" [level=3]:
        - link "Development of a Helmholtz free energy equation of state for fluid and solid phases via artificial neural networks":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01892-3
      - paragraph: The article presents an equation of state (EoS) for fluid and solid phases using artificial neural networks. This EoS accurately models thermophysical properties and predicts phase transitions, including the critical and triple points. This approach offers a unified way to understand different states of matter.
      - list:
        - listitem: Gustavo Chaparro
        - listitem: "& Erich A. Müller"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 19 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Room-temperature nonlinear transport and microwave rectification in antiferromagnetic MnBi2Te4 films" [level=3]:
        - link "Room-temperature nonlinear transport and microwave rectification in antiferromagnetic MnBi2Te4 films":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01897-y
          - text: Room-temperature nonlinear transport and microwave rectification in antiferromagnetic MnBi
          - subscript: "2"
          - text: Te
          - subscript: "4"
          - text: films
      - paragraph:
        - text: The nonlinear Hall effect enables studies of symmetry and topology with potential in high-frequency devices, but practical applications demand room temperature operation. The authors report robust room temperature nonlinear transverse responses and microwave rectification (1–8 GHz) in MnBi
        - subscript: "2"
        - text: Te
        - subscript: "4"
        - text: thin films, driven by extrinsic spin-orbit scattering.
      - list:
        - listitem: Shanshan Liu
        - listitem: ", Rhonald Burgos"
        - listitem: ... Kian Ping Loh
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 19 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Collective excitations and low-energy ionization signatures of relativistic particles in silicon detectors" [level=3]:
        - link "Collective excitations and low-energy ionization signatures of relativistic particles in silicon detectors":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01904-2
      - paragraph: The authors calculate the low-energy excitation cross section for relativistic feebly interacting particles scattering from silicon detectors. This enables a search for millicharged particles using data collected by the SENSEI detector and opens a new path for applications of low-threshold semi-conductor detectors to search for new physics.
      - list:
        - listitem: Rouven Essig
        - listitem: ", Ryan Plestid"
        - listitem: "& Aman Singal"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 19 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - 'heading "Reservoir direct feedback alignment: deep learning by physical dynamics" [level=3]':
        - 'link "Reservoir direct feedback alignment: deep learning by physical dynamics"':
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01895-0
      - paragraph: Existing training algorithms for deep neural networks are not suitable for energy-efficient analog hardware. Here, the authors propose and experimentally demonstrate an alternative training algorithm based on reservoir computing, which improves training efficiency in optoelectronic implementations.
      - list:
        - listitem: Mitsumasa Nakajima
        - listitem: ", Yongbo Zhang"
        - listitem: ... Kohei Nakajima
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 19 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Temporal-spatial manipulation of bi-focal bi-chromatic fields for terahertz radiations" [level=3]:
        - link "Temporal-spatial manipulation of bi-focal bi-chromatic fields for terahertz radiations":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01893-2
      - paragraph: Mixing the fundamental (ω) and the second harmonic (2ω) waves in the gas phase is a widely used technique for generating terahertz pulses. The authors experimentally present an enhanced terahertz emission through the temporal-spatial manipulation of bi-focal bi-chromatic fields, and the THz radiation mainly originates from the plasma created by the 2ω pulses instead of the ω pulses, which cannot be explained only using photocurrent model.
      - list:
        - listitem: Jingjing Zhao
        - listitem: ", Yizhu Zhang"
        - listitem: ... Yuhai Jiang
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 19 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Laser excitation of the 1S–2S transition in singly-ionized helium" [level=3]:
        - link "Laser excitation of the 1S–2S transition in singly-ionized helium":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01891-4
      - paragraph: A measurement of the 1S-2S transition frequency in He+ would enable fundamental physics tests, but the required extreme ultraviolet radiation makes this a challenge. The authors observe such transition using radiation produced by high-harmonic generation of frequency comb pulses, in a manner that is compatible with future precision spectroscopy.
      - list:
        - listitem: Elmer L. Gründeman
        - listitem: ", Vincent Barbé"
        - listitem: ... Kjeld S. E. Eikema
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 19 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Liquid-liquid phase separation driven by charge heterogeneity" [level=3]:
        - link "Liquid-liquid phase separation driven by charge heterogeneity":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01875-4
      - paragraph: Experiments show that charge heterogeneity in proteins affects their liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS). Using a theoretically grounded and numerically efficient coarse-grained model, the authors study how the amount of charge and its surface distribution affects the LLPS. They find that electrostatics controls the connectivity of particles thus impacting the emergence of the LLPS.
      - list:
        - listitem: Daniele Notarmuzi
        - listitem: "& Emanuela Bianchi"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 19 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Multi-field quantum conferencing overcomes the network capacity limit" [level=3]:
        - link "Multi-field quantum conferencing overcomes the network capacity limit":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01894-1
      - paragraph: Quantum networks require secure conference keys for users to communicate and decrypt broadcasts. The authors propose a quantum conferencing protocol that overcomes key rate limits in networks without repeaters by using post-measurement coincidence matching, enabling secure, efficient, and flexible communication resistant to detector side channel attacks.
      - list:
        - listitem: Yuan-Mei Xie
        - listitem: ", Yu-Shuo Lu"
        - listitem: ... Zeng-Bing Chen
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 19 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Reconstructing real-space geometries of polyatomic molecules undergoing strong field laser-induced Coulomb explosion" [level=3]:
        - link "Reconstructing real-space geometries of polyatomic molecules undergoing strong field laser-induced Coulomb explosion":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01863-8
      - paragraph: Understanding molecular structure and dynamics through strong-field laser interactions holds great promise. The authors use quantum calculations to show how bonds and angles evolve in an OCS molecule ionized six times by a 7 fs, 800 nm laser pulse, accurately predicting our experimental results.
      - list:
        - listitem: Aydin Ashrafi-Belgabad
        - listitem: ", Reza Karimi"
        - listitem: ... Joseph H. Sanderson
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 19 Dec 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Quantum valley Hall effect-based topological boundaries for frequency-dependent and -independent mode energy profiles" [level=3]:
        - link "Quantum valley Hall effect-based topological boundaries for frequency-dependent and -independent mode energy profiles":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01899-w
      - paragraph: The authors numerically and experimentally investigate the transport properties of a quantum valley-Hall effect in a micro electromechanical system. The zigzag and bridge boundaries, which have highly efficient wave transport, exhibit frequency independent and dependent wave localization, respectively.
      - list:
        - listitem: Keita Funayama
        - listitem: ", Kenichi Yatsugi"
        - listitem: "& Hideo Iizuka"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 19 Dec 2024

        - link "Suppressing unknown disturbances to dynamical systems using machine learning":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01885-2
      - paragraph: Identifying and mitigating unknown disturbances to complex systems poses a critical challenge in a wide range of disciplines. Here, the authors use machine learning to identify unknown disturbances made to unknown systems and a methodology to suppress these disturbances to recover the undisturbed system.
      - list:
        - listitem: Juan G. Restrepo
        - listitem: ", Clayton P. Byers"

      - heading "Online calibration of deep learning sub-models for hybrid numerical modeling systems" [level=3]:
        - link "Online calibration of deep learning sub-models for hybrid numerical modeling systems":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01880-7
      - paragraph: End-to-end learning in hybrid numerical models involves solving an optimization problem that integrates the model’s solver. In many fields, these solvers are written in low-abstraction programming languages that lack automatic differentiation. This work presents a practical approach to solving the optimization problem by efficiently approximating the gradient of the end-to-end objective function.
      - list:
        - listitem: Said Ouala

        - 'link "Cosmic entanglement sudden birth: expansion-induced entanglement in hydrogen atoms"':
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01907-z
      - paragraph: The authors investigate quantum entanglement in the hyperfine structure of the neutral hydrogen atom in thermal equilibrium with the cosmological microwave background radiation. They demonstrate that when the universe is around 80 billion years old, neutral hydrogen atoms begin to form entangled states, displaying a phenomenon known as entanglement sudden birth.
      - list:
        - listitem: Yusef Maleki
        - listitem: ", Alireza Maleki"
        - listitem: "& M. Suhail Zubairy"

        - link "A topological route to engineering robust and bright supersymmetric laser arrays":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01905-1
      - paragraph: In-phase synchronization of laser arrays remains one of the most important open problems in laser science. This work utilizes the relationship between chiral symmetric tight-binding models and supersymmetry to engineer a near-uniform laser array with a superior far-field intensity scaling, extending the frontiers of laser technology.
      - list:

        - listitem: ", Mohammadmahdi Alizadeh"

    - article:
      - heading "Circuit-noise-resilient virtual distillation" [level=3]:
        - link "Circuit-noise-resilient virtual distillation":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01815-2
      - paragraph: This study focuses on reducing noise in the circuit used in the quantum error mitigation method called Virtual Distillation (VD). The authors introduce an approach which significantly enhances the noise tolerance of VD and improves the accuracy by an order of magnitude compared to the standard VD.
      - list:
        - listitem: Xiao-Yue Xu
        - listitem: ", Chen Ding"
        - listitem: ... He-Liang Huang
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 09 Oct 2024
    - article:
      - 'heading "Hydride units filled boron–carbon clathrate: a pathway for high-temperature superconductivity at ambient pressure" [level=3]':
        - 'link "Hydride units filled boron–carbon clathrate: a pathway for high-temperature superconductivity at ambient pressure"':
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01814-3
      - paragraph: The quest for room-temperature superconductivity has been a long-standing aspiration and a central focus of research in the field of condensed matter physics. Here, the authors propose integrating hydride units into Boron-Carbon clathrate structures to achieve high-temperature superconductivity at ambient pressure.
      - list:
        - listitem: Ying Sun
        - listitem: "& Li Zhu"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 08 Oct 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Scalable on-chip multiplexing of silicon single and double quantum dots" [level=3]:
        - link "Scalable on-chip multiplexing of silicon single and double quantum dots":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01806-3
      - paragraph: The integration of quantum dot spin qubits and classical cryogenic microelectronics is important for scaling up silicon-based quantum computers. The authors show that their silicon technology tailored for low-power electronics and low-noise quantum dots enables the integration of classical multiplexers and quantum dot spin qubit devices on the same chip.
      - list:
        - listitem: Heorhii Bohuslavskyi
        - listitem: ", Alberto Ronzani"
        - listitem: ... Mika Prunnila
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 07 Oct 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Mitigating noise in digital and digital–analog quantum computation" [level=3]:
        - link "Mitigating noise in digital and digital–analog quantum computation":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01812-5
      - paragraph: The authors explore the digital-analog quantum computing paradigm, which combines fast single-qubit gates with the natural dynamics of quantum devices. They find the digital-analog paradigm more robust against certain experimental imperfections than the standard fully-digital one and successfully apply error mitigation techniques to this approach.
      - list:
        - listitem: Paula García-Molina
        - listitem: ", Ana Martin"
        - listitem: ... Mikel Sanz
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 06 Oct 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Quantum state tomography with locally purified density operators and local measurements" [level=3]:
        - link "Quantum state tomography with locally purified density operators and local measurements":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01813-4
      - paragraph: Quantum state tomography is a fundamental tool for assessing the performance of quantum hardware and plays a crucial role in advancing quantum information processing. The authors present a method based on tensor network representations and local measurements, demonstrating accuracy and efficiency in characterizing noisy quantum states.
      - list:
        - listitem: Yuchen Guo
        - listitem: "& Shuo Yang"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 06 Oct 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Low-loss metasurfaces based on discretized meta-atoms" [level=3]:
        - link "Low-loss metasurfaces based on discretized meta-atoms":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01808-1
      - paragraph: Metasurfaces are established tools for manipulating light and enhancing light-matter interactions, but the loss of conventional meta-atoms usually limits the performance potential of metasurfaces. Here, the authors propose a class of metasurfaces based on discretized meta-atoms able to mitigate the radiative and intrinsic losses, as interpreted by their built coupling model.
      - list:
        - listitem: Yisheng Gao
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 05 Oct 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Topological protection revealed by real-time longitudinal and transverse transport measurements" [level=3]:
        - link "Topological protection revealed by real-time longitudinal and transverse transport measurements":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01800-9
      - paragraph: Understanding the mechanisms influencing the robustness of topologically protected states is of fundamental relevance. This experimental work demonstrates, through the observation of real-time longitudinal and transverse responses, the importance of transverse reconstruction of protected modes which is influenced by electron-electron interaction in addition to disorder.
      - list:
        - listitem: Hoai Anh Ho
        - listitem: ", Jian Huang"
        - listitem: ... K. W. West
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 04 Oct 2024
    - article:
      - 'heading "Kitaev honeycomb antiferromagnet in a field: quantum phase diagram for general spin" [level=3]':
        - 'link "Kitaev honeycomb antiferromagnet in a field: quantum phase diagram for general spin"':
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01809-0
      - paragraph: The antiferromagnetic spin 1/2 Kitaev model is known to have an intermediate phase under a magnetic field before transitioning to a fully polarized state. However, the nature of this phase for higher spins remained unclear. This paper explores the quantum phase diagram of the antiferromagnetic Kitaev honeycomb model in a magnetic field using tensor-network methods and high-order linked cluster expansions, uncovering an intermediate phase with distinct local magnetization patterns across different spin values.
      - list:
        - listitem: Saeed S. Jahromi
        - listitem: ", Max Hörmann"
        - listitem: ... Kai Phillip Schmidt

      - heading "Mercury’s plasma environment after BepiColombo’s third flyby" [level=3]:
        - link "Mercury’s plasma environment after BepiColombo’s third flyby":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01766-8
      - paragraph:
        - text: Due to its proximity to the Sun, the space plasma environment of Mercury is tightly coupled with the interior and the surface of the planet, and their interaction facilitate the escape of planetary material and energy exchange. The authors present data from the third flyby of the BepiColombo spacecraft revealing new evidence of trapped energetic hydrogen (H
        - superscript: +
        - text: ) with energies of around 20 keV/e and highlight the presence of cold ion population below 50 eV/e in Mercury’s magnetosphere.
      - list:
        - listitem: Lina Z. Hadid
        - listitem: ", Dominique Delcourt"
        - listitem: ... Shoya Matsuda
      - generic: Article

      - time: 03 Oct 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Atomic-scale imaging of laser-driven electron dynamics in solids" [level=3]:
        - link "Atomic-scale imaging of laser-driven electron dynamics in solids":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01810-7
      - paragraph: Manipulation of materials properties by laser driving can lead to future technological applications, but a complete picture of its mechanisms is missing. In their paper, authors propose a method based on ultrafast x-ray diffraction that allows for resolving laser-driven electron dynamics on their natural time and length scales.
      - list:
        - listitem: Daria Popova-Gorelova
        - listitem: "& Robin Santra"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 02 Oct 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Gate tunable edge magnetoplasmon resonators" [level=3]:
        - link "Gate tunable edge magnetoplasmon resonators":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01803-6
      - paragraph: Edge-magnetoplasmon interferometers have been proposed as a tool to investigate anyonic properties of quasiparticles in the regime of the Fractional Quantum Hall effect. In this work, the authors demonstrate the possibility to control electrostatically the resonance frequency of EMP resonators of micrometric size and explain the role of gates, paving the way toward the realization of anyonic interferometers.
      - list:
        - listitem: Elric Frigerio
        - listitem: ", Giacomo Rebora"
        - listitem: ... Gerbold C. Ménard
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access

      - heading "Photonic counterdiabatic quantum optimization algorithm" [level=3]:
        - link "Photonic counterdiabatic quantum optimization algorithm":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01807-2
      - paragraph: The authors introduce a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for photonic quantum computing that focuses on tackling continuous-variable optimization problems using fewer quantum operations than existing methods. The approach shows better performance and practical implementation potential, demonstrated on Xanadu’s quantum chip.
      - list:

      - time: 30 Sept 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Spontaneous reversal of spin chirality and competing phases in the topological magnet EuAl4" [level=3]:
        - link "Spontaneous reversal of spin chirality and competing phases in the topological magnet EuAl4":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01802-7
          - text: Spontaneous reversal of spin chirality and competing phases in the topological magnet EuAl
          - subscript: "4"
      - paragraph: The reversal of spin chirality in the absence of any externally applied field would substantially broaden the use of chiral magnets for applications in spintronic devices. In this manuscript the authors demonstrate the spontaneous reversal of spin chirality in the topological magnet EuAl4 using resonant elastic x-ray scattering.

    - article:
      - heading "Droplets can enhance microcapsule deformation in channel flow" [level=3]:
        - link "Droplets can enhance microcapsule deformation in channel flow":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01805-4
      - paragraph: Enhancing deformation of soft microparticles such as cells, capsules and vesicles has widespread applications in cell phenotyping, drug/gene delivery and smart material synthesis. Here, the authors demonstrate that enclosing a capsule into a droplet can amplify the capsule deformation parameter by up to two orders of magnitude, compared with an isolated capsule experiencing identical channel flow conditions.
      - list:
        - listitem: Dalei Jing
        - listitem: ", Ruixin Lu"
        - listitem: ... Yi Sui

      - time: 20 Sept 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Constraints on fifth forces and ultralight dark matter from OSIRIS-REx target asteroid Bennu" [level=3]:
        - link "Constraints on fifth forces and ultralight dark matter from OSIRIS-REx target asteroid Bennu":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01779-3
      - paragraph: Asteroid tracking has been demonstrated as a promising and prominent probe of fifth forces arising in several well-motivated models beyond the Standard Model of particle physics. The authors use the state-of-art tracking data for the asteroid Bennu from the OSIRIS-REx mission to derive the tightest limits on fifth forces and ultralight dark matter at the lengths of solar-system objects.
      - list:
        - listitem: Yu-Dai Tsai
        - listitem: ", Davide Farnocchia"
        - listitem: ... Luca Visinelli
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 20 Sept 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Emergence of group size disparity in growing networks with adoption" [level=3]:
        - link "Emergence of group size disparity in growing networks with adoption":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01799-z
      - paragraph: The authors introduce a network growth and adoption model with preferential attachment and asymmetric mixing that can explain the inequalities observed in the group growth dynamics in scientific citation and collaboration. This model can be used to investigate the effect of intervention in group mixing preferences to overcome cumulative disparities.
      - list:
        - listitem: Jun Sun
        - listitem: "& Fariba Karimi"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 19 Sept 2024

        - 'link "Designer spin-orbit superlattices: symmetry-protected Dirac cones and spin Berry curvature in two-dimensional van der Waals metamaterials"':
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01801-8
      - paragraph: Engineering sizeable spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in graphene generates effects unmatched in traditional low-dimensional systems. Here, the authors show that the periodic modulation of SOC in 1D patterned graphene heterostructures leads to unusual mini-band structures with symmetry-protected Dirac cones featuring enhanced spin Berry curvature, which paves the way to tunable spin Hall responses.
      - list:
        - listitem: L. M. Martelo
        - listitem: "& Aires Ferreira"

        - link "Purification scheduling control for throughput maximization in quantum networks":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01796-2
      - paragraph: In quantum networks, entanglement purification is required to ensure that the E2E fidelity of the entanglement connections can support quantum applications reliably. Here, the authors explore the purification resource scheduling problem from a network-level perspective by jointly optimizing purification and resource allocation processes to maximize the throughput under the fidelity requirement.

      - paragraph: Droplet dynamics on lubricated surfaces differ fundamentally from those on dry surfaces due to the formation of a wetting ridge around the droplet.       - paragraph: A class of urn-based models accounts for stochastic regularities observed in systems that exhibit innovation in diverse forms and temporal scales, from the appearance of new organisms to the evolution of language to daily new experiences.         - link "Experimental observation of violent relaxation":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01684-9
      - paragraph: Large structure in the Universe, such as galaxies, are believed to form by a process called violent relaxation, which occurs over millions of years. The authors present a nonlinear optics experiment which shows direct observation of violent relaxation, whose evolution can be related to the equations governing galaxy formation.

        - link "Topological order from measurements and feed-forward on a trapped ion quantum computer":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01698-3
      - paragraph: Topological quantum states are essential resources in quantum error correction and quantum simulation but unitary quantum circuits for their preparation require extensive circuit depth. The authors demonstrate a constant-depth protocol to prepare topologically ordered states on a trapped-ion quantum computer using non-unitary operations.

          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01696-5
      - paragraph: This paper presents a study on topologically enhanced third harmonic generation within resonant nonlinear topolectrical circuits. The authors demonstrate that the implementation of a mirror-stacking approach in one-dimensional topological circuits enables achieving significant harmonic wave power increase, leading to efficient nonlinear processes.

      - paragraph: The study of the general factors underlying clogging are fragmented and application-driven due to its broad spectrum of applications.       - paragraph: Recent theoretical works have predicted lasing/condensation in multimode exciton-polaritons, hybrid light-matter quasiparticles, but the origin and the dynamics of multimode condensation has not been experimentally investigated.       - paragraph: This research explores how incident angles affect topological phase transitions in one-dimensional photonic crystals, impacting both TE and TM polarized modes.       - paragraph: The trajectory of the active droplets in an isotropic environment can be controlled by gradients of chemicals, physical obstacles, or by electric fields, but these methods are either static, transient, or require a complicated design.       - paragraph: "Complex networks composed of interacting oscillators are frequently characterized by two features: adaptivity and cluster synchronization.       - paragraph: Mechanical bound states in the continuum (BICs) offer a novel approach for realizing high-frequency, high-Q mechanical resonators.       - paragraph: Originally developed in the context of ecology, the dimension reduction approach allows to study the dynamics of complex systems at large scale, while retaining the interaction patterns within the system.       - heading "Reconfigurable synthetic dimension frequency lattices in an integrated lithium niobate ring cavity" [level=3]:
        - link "Reconfigurable synthetic dimension frequency lattices in an integrated lithium niobate ring cavity":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01676-9
      - paragraph: Lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) is emerging as a powerful photonic integration platform for synthetic dimension approaches that enable probing of higher-dimensional physical models within low-dimensional devices. The authors present a LNOI ring device, whose frequency modes represent lattice sites for versatile simulation of tight-binding models with up to three-dimensional connectivity.
      - list:
        - listitem: Hiep X. Dinh
        - listitem: ", Armandas Balčytis"

      - heading "Unveiling universal aspects of the cellular anatomy of the brain" [level=3]:
        - link "Unveiling universal aspects of the cellular anatomy of the brain":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01665-y
      - paragraph: Cellular-level partial brain reconstructions have revealed the anatomic complexity of the brains of multiple organisms. Here, the authors quantify aspects of this complexity, demonstrating that across organisms the cellular structure of the brain shows universal scaling properties associated with being in the vicinity of criticality.
      - list:
        - listitem: Helen S. Ansell
        - listitem: "& István A. Kovács"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 10 Jun 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Dynamic metastable vortex states in interacting vortex lines" [level=3]:
        - link "Dynamic metastable vortex states in interacting vortex lines":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01645-2
      - paragraph: Vortex motion defines transport properties of type II superconductors. Here, authors study the effect of vortex synchronisation with an external periodic drive, that leads to the effects of integer and fractional Shapiro steps and even creates metastable states.
      - list:
        - listitem: Sergei Kozlov
        - listitem: ", Jérôme Lesueur"
        - listitem: ... Cheryl Feuillet-Palma
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 08 Jun 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Discovery of charge order above room-temperature in the prototypical kagome superconductor La(Ru1−xFex)3Si2" [level=3]:
        - link "Discovery of charge order above room-temperature in the prototypical kagome superconductor La(Ru1−xFex)3Si2":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01673-y
          - text: Discovery of charge order above room-temperature in the prototypical kagome superconductor La(Ru
          - subscript: 1−x
          - text: Fe
          - subscript: x
          - text: )
          - subscript: "3"
          - text: Si
          - subscript: "2"
      - paragraph: The study focuses on the charge order in LaRu3Si2, a material with a kagome lattice structure, discovering a charge-ordered state that persists at or above room temperature. This finding classifies LaRu3Si2 as the kagome superconductor with the highest charge ordering temperature, suggesting potential for applications in devices operating at normal environmental conditions without the need for cooling.
      - list:
        - listitem: I. Plokhikh
        - listitem: ", C. Mielke III"
        - listitem: ... Z. Guguchia
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 08 Jun 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Density profile of 3He in a nanoscale 3He-4He superfluid film determined by neutron scattering" [level=3]:
        - link "Density profile of 3He in a nanoscale 3He-4He superfluid film determined by neutron scattering":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01683-w
          - text: Density profile of
          - superscript: "3"
          - text: He in a nanoscale
          - superscript: "3"
          - text: He-
          - superscript: "4"
          - text: He superfluid film determined by neutron scattering
      - paragraph: Superfluidity, a liquid exhibiting frictionless flow, is so far limited to observations in low-temperature 3He and 4He, where the underlying mechanisms governing the quantum state are complex and different for each isotope, making for a fascinating but challenging phenomenon to study experimentally. The authors use isotope-sensitive neutron reflectometry to investigate mixed 3He/4He superfluid He films on a Si surface, and resolve the structural features and phase transitions that occur with changing temperature.
      - list:
        - listitem: Oleg Kirichek
        - listitem: ", Christopher R. Lawson"
        - listitem: ... Peter V. E. McClintock
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 07 Jun 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Magnetic Dirac semimetal state of (Mn,Ge)Bi2Te4" [level=3]:
        - link "Magnetic Dirac semimetal state of (Mn,Ge)Bi2Te4":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01675-w
          - text: Magnetic Dirac semimetal state of (Mn,Ge)Bi
          - subscript: "2"
          - text: Te
          - subscript: "4"
      - paragraph:
        - text: Topological insulators with ordered moments of embedded magnetic atoms are viable platforms for quantum electronics, but the practical applications are restricted by the size of their crystals. The authors synthesize a Z2 topological insulator Ge
        - subscript: x
        - text: Mn
        - subscript: 1-x
        - text: Bi
        - subscript: "2"
        - text: Te
        - subscript: "4"
        - text: in the form of a large crystal with high structural perfection and tunable magnetic and electronic properties.

        - listitem: ... Lada V. Yashina
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 05 Jun 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Quasi-localization and Wannier obstruction in partially flat bands" [level=3]:
        - link "Quasi-localization and Wannier obstruction in partially flat bands":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01679-6
      - paragraph: Compact localized states constitute an auxiliary state representation for a flat-band lattice system with wave functions non-zero only in a finite portion of the lattice. Here, the authors show that in some flat-band systems, these states can be partially “hidden”; surprisingly, these ghost flat bands present an obstruction to be represented as maximally localized Wannier functions.
      - list:
        - listitem: Jin-Hong Park
        - listitem: "& Jun-Won Rhim"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 04 Jun 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Monolithic optical resonator for ultrastable laser and photonic millimeter-wave synthesis" [level=3]:
        - link "Monolithic optical resonator for ultrastable laser and photonic millimeter-wave synthesis":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01660-3
      - paragraph: Optical resonators are essential tools for high precision metrology and applications where the spectral purity is highly demanded. Here, the authors demonstrate a monolithic resonator made of fused silica to support 18 Hz integrated laser linewidth in the ambient environment, and W-band microwave generation with low phase noise of -100 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz frequency offset.
      - list:
        - listitem: Wei Zhang
        - listitem: ", Eric Kittlaus"
        - listitem: ... Andrey Matsko
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 04 Jun 2024
    - article:
      - 'heading "Accurate hyperfine tensors for solid state quantum applications: case of the NV center in diamond" [level=3]':
        - 'link "Accurate hyperfine tensors for solid state quantum applications: case of the NV center in diamond"':
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01668-9
      - paragraph: Hyperfine interaction is the key term for utilizing individual nuclear spins in solids. This work introduces a method that yields high-accuracy hyperfine values for nuclear spins at arbitrary distances from addressable electron spins, such as the NV center in diamond.
      - list:
        - listitem: István Takács
        - listitem: "& Viktor Ivády"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 04 Jun 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Concurrence of directional Kondo transport and incommensurate magnetic order in the layered material AgCrSe2" [level=3]:
        - link "Concurrence of directional Kondo transport and incommensurate magnetic order in the layered material AgCrSe2":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01671-0
          - text: Concurrence of directional Kondo transport and incommensurate magnetic order in the layered material AgCrSe
          - subscript: "2"
      - paragraph:
        - text: This study reports on the simultaneous emergence of the impurity Kondo effect and incommensurate magnetic ordering in the layered material AgCrSe
        - subscript: "2"
        - text: these usually mutually exclusive phenomena complement each other. The ability to enable Kondo effect in association with the antiferromagnetic order, provides a novel route to tune the competition between magnetic correlations and Kondo screening.
      - list:
        - listitem: José Guimarães
        - listitem: ", Dorsa S. Fartab"
        - listitem: ... Haijing Zhang
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 01 Jun 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Higher-order non-Markovian social contagions in simplicial complexes" [level=3]:
        - link "Higher-order non-Markovian social contagions in simplicial complexes":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01666-x
      - paragraph: High-order structures are ubiquitous in numerous real-world networks and play a significant role in social contagion phenomena, the authors introduce a novel higher-order non-Markovian social contagion model, addressing limitations of traditional models. Through mean-field theory and simulations, the authors demonstrate that there is an equivalence between the higher-order non-Markovian and the higher-order Markovian social contagions and reveal the resilience enhancement conferred by non-Markovian recovery, shedding light on real-world contagion dynamics.
      - list:
        - listitem: Zhaohua Lin
        - listitem: ", Lilei Han"
        - listitem: ... Ming Tang
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 01 Jun 2024
    - article:
      - 'heading "Deep-learning-based decomposition of overlapping-sparse images: application at the vertex of simulated neutrino interactions" [level=3]':
        - 'link "Deep-learning-based decomposition of overlapping-sparse images: application at the vertex of simulated neutrino interactions"':
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01669-8
      - paragraph: The paper addresses the task of extracting individual objects from multi-dimensional overlapping-sparse images, with valuable impact in high-energy physics (future high-precision long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments). The developed tool will allow to reduce systematic errors and avoid model dependence, improving the neutrino energy resolution and sensitivity.
      - list:
        - listitem: Saúl Alonso-Monsalve
        - listitem: ", Davide Sgalaberna"
        - listitem: ... André Rubbia
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 01 Jun 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Quantum force sensing by digital twinning of atomic Bose-Einstein condensates" [level=3]:
        - link "Quantum force sensing by digital twinning of atomic Bose-Einstein condensates":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01662-1
      - paragraph: In this study, the authors propose a generic machine-learning-assisted framework to improve the overall performance of quantum sensing application. In the context of an atomic force sensor, this entirely data-driven approach, which involves generating the digital twinning of experimental data, demonstrates an order of magnitude improvement in sensitivity compared to conventional protocols.
      - list:
        - listitem: Tangyou Huang
        - listitem: ", Zhongcheng Yu"
        - listitem: ... Xiaopeng Li
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 01 Jun 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Control of cell membrane receptor condensation by adhesion to supported bilayers with nanoscale topography" [level=3]:
        - link "Control of cell membrane receptor condensation by adhesion to supported bilayers with nanoscale topography":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01670-1
      - paragraph: Developing physical methods to modulate biomolecular condensates on cell membranes is of great importance for understanding physiological processes and stimulating novel therapeutic strategies. We propose an effective means to control receptor condensation on cell membranes via adhesion to a supported lipid bilayer with nanoscale topography.
      - list:
        - listitem: Long Li
        - listitem: ", Ruihan Hou"
        - listitem: ... Fan Song

      - time: 01 Jun 2024

      - heading "Resource theory of imaginarity in distributed scenarios" [level=3]:
        - link "Resource theory of imaginarity in distributed scenarios":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01649-y
      - paragraph: This work examines imaginarity as a resource in quantum information theory. The authors extend the resource theory of imaginarity to distributed scenarios, discuss the operational meaning and its role in channel discrimination.
      - list:
        - listitem: Kang-Da Wu
        - listitem: ", Tulja Varun Kondra"
        - listitem: ... Alexander Streltsov
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 31 May 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Local dominance unveils clusters in networks" [level=3]:
        - link "Local dominance unveils clusters in networks":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01635-4
      - paragraph: Community detection has been studied for more than 20 years, but a perspective from community center is still missing and most algorithms need global information. The authors propose a linear algorithm based on local information to identify centers and related hierarchical structure for effective community detection, which can enhance clustering vector data as well.
      - list:
        - listitem: Dingyi Shi
        - listitem: ", Fan Shang"
        - listitem: ... Ruiqi Li
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 31 May 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Yukawa-Lorentz symmetry in non-Hermitian Dirac materials" [level=3]:
        - link "Yukawa-Lorentz symmetry in non-Hermitian Dirac materials":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01629-2
      - paragraph: Lorentz symmetry plays a fundamental role in classical to quantum electrodynamics, as well as in quantum chromodynamics, which is typically realized at sufficiently high energies and often exclusively in closed or isolated quantum systems. Here, the authors show that such a fundamental space–time symmetry can also be manifest as an emergent symmetry even in open Dirac systems, when they interact with the surrounding environment.
      - list:
        - listitem: Vladimir Juričić
        - listitem: "& Bitan Roy"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 27 May 2024
    - article:
      - heading "On-demand photonic Ising machine with simplified Hamiltonian calculation by phase encoding and intensity detection" [level=3]:
        - link "On-demand photonic Ising machine with simplified Hamiltonian calculation by phase encoding and intensity detection":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01658-x
      - paragraph: Photonic Ising machines exploit the parallelism and high propagation speed of light to solve combinatorial optimization tasks. The authors propose and demonstrate a photonic Ising machine with a fully reconfigurable optical vector-matrix transformation system and a modified algorithm based on simulated annealing, solving 20 and 30-spin Ising problems with high ground state probability.
      - list:
        - listitem: Jiayi Ouyang
        - listitem: ", Yuxuan Liao"
        - listitem: ... Yidong Huang
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 24 May 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Excitable dynamics driven by mechanical feedback in biological tissues" [level=3]:
        - link "Excitable dynamics driven by mechanical feedback in biological tissues":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01661-2
      - paragraph: Many excitable systems share a common feedback motif, but how such feedback acts on biomechanical systems remains largely unexplored. By extending the cellular vertex models to incorporate mechanochemical feedback and excitability, the authors explore how cellular mechanics and geometry regulate the propagation of active stresses in excitable media.
      - list:

        - listitem: ", Samuel Banks"
        - listitem: "& Shiladitya Banerjee"
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access

          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01659-w
      - paragraph: Solitons are nonlinear, stable and coherent solitary wave structures that have been investigated in a variety of systems from optics to plasma physics. The authors experimentally and theoretically investigate the dynamics of soliton arrays in a two-component Bose-Einstein condensate.

      - heading "Enhanced quantum coherence of plasmonic resonances with a chiral exceptional points" [level=3]:
        - link "Enhanced quantum coherence of plasmonic resonances with a chiral exceptional points":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01655-0
      - paragraph: The advent of non-Hermitian optics carries new possibilities in manipulating optical response, offering alternative ways to enhance the quantum coherence of plasmonic resonances. Based on a theoretical model, the authors calculate a quantum yield enhanced by two orders of magnitude at room temperature, achieved by integration of a plasmonic antenna in a photonic cavity operated at a chiral exceptional point.
      - list:
        - listitem: Yu-Wei Lu
        - listitem: ", Jing-Feng Liu"

      - heading "Observation of a phase space horizon with surface gravity water waves" [level=3]:
        - link "Observation of a phase space horizon with surface gravity water waves":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01616-7
      - paragraph: Since 1974, it was theoretically postulated that black holes, despite their name, emit radiation with a spectrum like that of a black body. Utilizing surface gravity water waves to emulate black hole physics, the authors reveal the emergence of a logarithmic phase singularity analogous to that predicted by Hawking in black holes, whose energy distribution associated with the singularity results in a Fermi-Dirac distribution instead of the familiar Bose-Einstein statistics of the Hawking radiation.
      - list:
        - listitem: Georgi Gary Rozenman
        - listitem: ", Freyja Ullinger"
        - listitem: ... Ady Arie

      - heading "Si-CMOS compatible epsilon-near-zero metamaterial for two-color ultrafast all-optical switching" [level=3]:
        - link "Si-CMOS compatible epsilon-near-zero metamaterial for two-color ultrafast all-optical switching":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01654-1
      - paragraph: Epsilon-near-zero materials are promising to realize ultrafast all-optical devices, but their integration into photonic chips requires simultaneously wide broadband operativity, low-losses and Si-compatiblity. The authors propose a Si-compatible multilayer metamaterial capable of all-optical switching response times of few hundred femtoseconds.
      - list:
        - listitem: Alessandro Pianelli
        - listitem: ", Rakesh Dhama"
        - listitem: ... Humeyra Caglayan
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 22 May 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Large anomalous Hall conductivity induced by spin chirality fluctuation in an ultraclean frustrated antiferromagnet PdCrO2" [level=3]:
        - link "Large anomalous Hall conductivity induced by spin chirality fluctuation in an ultraclean frustrated antiferromagnet PdCrO2":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01652-3
          - text: Large anomalous Hall conductivity induced by spin chirality fluctuation in an ultraclean frustrated antiferromagnet PdCrO
          - subscript: "2"
      - paragraph:
        - text: Magnetic frustration of spins often leads to nontrivial spin textures and anomalous Hall responses, but typically below the magnetic transition temperature. The authors observe a giant unconventional anomalous Hall conductivity in the triangularlattice antiferromagnet PdCrO
        - subscript: "2"
        - text: well above its Neel temperature, attributed to spin cluster skew scattering.
      - list:
        - listitem: Hoseong Jeon
        - listitem: ", Hyeongwoo Seo"
        - listitem: ... Jun Sung Kim
      - generic: Article

      - time: 21 May 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Confirming the theoretical foundation of steady-state microbunching" [level=3]:
        - link "Confirming the theoretical foundation of steady-state microbunching":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01657-y
      - paragraph: Steady-State Microbunching (SSMB) is emerging as a new concept for accelerator-based light sources to meet demands for high average power radiation at short wavelengths. The authors present findings from a proof-of-principle experiment that agree with theoretical expectations in multiple aspects, laying the foundation for the future realization of SSMB.
      - list:
        - listitem: Arnold Kruschinski
        - listitem: ", Xiujie Deng"
        - listitem: ... Alexander Chao
      - generic: Article
      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 21 May 2024
    - article:
      - heading "Nonlinear dynamics of femtosecond laser interaction with the central nervous system in zebrafish" [level=3]:
        - link "Nonlinear dynamics of femtosecond laser interaction with the central nervous system in zebrafish":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01653-2
      - paragraph: When a pulsed laser interacts with tissue, the molecules in the sample get excited to a higher energy state and relax either nonradiatively, leading to thermal damage, or via de-excitation processes, frequently associated with photodamage. Here, the authors explore how different photodamage mechanisms unfold across a spectrum of intense near-infrared femtosecond pulses.
      - list:
        - listitem: Soyeon Jun
        - listitem: ", Andreas Herbst"
        - listitem: ... Hanieh Fattahi

      - generic: Open Access
      - time: 21 May 2024

      - heading "Enhanced emergent electromagnetic inductance in Tb5Sb3 due to highly disordered helimagnetism" [level=3]:

          - text: Sb
          - subscript: "3"
          - text: due to highly disordered helimagnetism
      - paragraph:
        - text: Ac current-driven spin motions in helimagnetic metals can generate emergent electric fields acting on conduction electrons, leading to emergent electromagnetic induction (EEMI). In this study, we revealed that a short-period helimagnet Tb
        - subscript: "5"
        - text: Sb
        - subscript: "3"
        - text: may have disordered spin helix structure and provides large EEMI.

          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01651-4
      - paragraph: Recently ideal spin filtering ability was demonstrated in the Dy-L-Tar metal-organic framework. In this work the authors show that this unusual effect emerges from the asymmetric display of alpha and beta spin states around the Fermi level, composed of the f states of the lanthanide.

      - heading "Bursting of condensates" [level=3]:
        - link "Bursting of condensates":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01650-5
      - paragraph: Condensates with a shell can be formed by liquid-liquid phase separation and can burst like viscous bubbles by nucleation and growth of a hole in the shell surrounded by a rim. The authors develop a model to extract a broad range of rheological properties for spherical shells to understand the conditions for bursting.

          - text: Orbital-overlap-driven hybridization in 3d-transition metal perovskite oxides LaMO

      - heading "Testing structural balance theories in heterogeneous signed networks" [level=3]:
        - link "Testing structural balance theories in heterogeneous signed networks":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01640-7
      - paragraph: "According to balance theory, social actors avoid establishing cycles with an odd number of negative links. This statement can be supported only after a comparison with a benchmark. The authors find that the level of balance depends on the null-model employed: homogeneous ones favor the weak balance theory; heterogeneous ones favor the strong balance theory."

        - link "Biased versus unbiased numerical methods for stochastic simulations":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01648-z
      - paragraph: The binomial method, and similar approximations, are often used for numerical simulations of population models in mathematical epidemiology and ecology. The authors study the binomial method to approximate a stochastic dynamic and compare it with an unbiased Gillespie method for stochastic simulation deriving insights on optimal discretization schemes for the binomial method and provide corresponding rules that would indicate if binomial or unbiased solution methods are more efficient.

          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01637-2
      - paragraph: In many chiral particle systems, vortex patterns emerge in the velocity fields due to the alignment interactions, but these patterns are non-permanent and decohere quickly. The authors predict the spontaneous emergence of vortices with high dynamical coherence, and identify the transition between the regimes of constant and oscillating vorticity.

          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01646-1
      - paragraph: Despite the numerous analogies between (non)Brownian suspensions and pedestrian crowds, rheological studies on the dynamics of the latter are scarce. Adopting such rheological perspective, the authors show that contact forces alone cannot lead to the faster-is-slower effect, but that social force interactions need to be included.

        - link "Large impact of phonon lineshapes on the superconductivity of solid hydrogen":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01643-4
      - paragraph: This work studies the effects of non-gaussian phonon lineshapes from stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation on the superconducting critical temperature (Tc) of hydrogen at high pressure. It predicts superconductivity in the Cmca-12 phase between 450 and 500 GPa and an increase in Tc for both the Cmca-12 and the I41/amd-2 structures compared to harmonic calculations.

        - link "Stoichiometric control of electron mobility and 2D superconductivity at LaAlO3-SrTiO3 interfaces":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01644-3
          - text: Stoichiometric control of electron mobility and 2D superconductivity at LaAlO

          - subscript: "3"

      - paragraph:
        - text: SrTiO
        - subscript: "3"
        - text: "-based oxide interfaces, which exhibit coexistence of gate-tunable two-dimensional superconductivity and Rashba spin-orbit coupling, are candidates to host topological superconductive phases. By controlling the chemical ratio in LaAlO"
        - subscript: "3"
        - text: ", the authors demonstrate tuning of carrier densities, mobilities and the formation of superconductivity, showing that, approaching to clean limit, significant enhancement below the Lifshitz transition is observed, at odds with previous experimental investigations."
      - list:

        - listitem: ", Roger Guzman"

        - link "Spacetime magnetic hopfions from internal excitations and braiding of skyrmions":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01628-3
      - paragraph: Topological solitons are localized structures whose stability emerges from the topology of their spatial structure, hence they are usually independent of the temporal dimension. The authors construct topological magnetic solitons in space-time from periodically driven magnetic structures that can be externally controlled.
      - list:

        - listitem: ... Karin Everschor-Sitte

    - article:
      - heading "Polarization-independent Spatial Kramers-Kronig medium for omnidirectional reflectionless absorption of unpolarized light" [level=3]:
        - link "Polarization-independent Spatial Kramers-Kronig medium for omnidirectional reflectionless absorption of unpolarized light":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01639-0
      - paragraph: Spatial Kramers–Kronig (KK) media are inhomogeneous materials enabling omnidirectional light absorption, but the successful experimental realizations are polarization-dependent, i.e., they absorb either transverse electric or transverse magnetic fields. Using a matryoshka metamaterial, the authors report the experimental realization of a polarization-independent omnidirectional absorber.
      - list:
        - listitem: Quanping Li
        - listitem: ", Yu Luo"
        - listitem: ... Dexin Ye

      - heading "Neural-network quantum states for ultra-cold Fermi gases" [level=3]:
        - link "Neural-network quantum states for ultra-cold Fermi gases":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01613-w
      - paragraph: The theoretical description of ultra-cold Fermi gases is challenging due to the presence of strong, short-ranged interactions. This work introduces a Pfaffian-Jastrow neural-network quantum state that outperforms existing Slater-Jastrow frameworks and diffusion Monte Carlo methods.
      - list:

        - listitem: ", Gabriel Pescia"
        - listitem: ... Alessandro Lovato

      - generic: Open Access

    - article:
      - heading "Chiral limit and origin of topological flat bands in twisted transition metal dichalcogenide homobilayers" [level=3]:
        - link "Chiral limit and origin of topological flat bands in twisted transition metal dichalcogenide homobilayers":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01641-6
      - paragraph: The strongly correlated interactions found in twisted bilayer systems give rise to a range of exotic phenomena but due to range of factors it is challenging to develop theoretical models that can faithfully describe the underlying physics. Here, the authors provide an analysis of the chiral limits of perturbed Dirac field theories that are relevant to C3-symmetric twisted bilayer graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides homobilayers. They identify two possible scenarios and show that flat bands are a more likely phenomenon in the latter system

      - paragraph: Silicon carbide polytypes (SiC) exhibit second-order optic nonlinearity to act as on-chip nonlinear and quantum light sources, but their integration is typically challenging.       - paragraph: The next generation of high energy particle colliders will have features that allows for highly granular detectors and current methods for particle collision reconstruction are limited.       - paragraph: While its museums are adorned by the masterpieces born from the brushes of Klimt and Schiele, the steps of prominent scientists like Hess, Boltzmann, and Schrödinger still echo in the halls of its university.       - paragraph: The magnetospheric multiscale mission (MMS) consists of four identical spacecraft used to collect data on the interaction between the Sun and Earth’s magnetic fields and study how the various interactions govern the dynamics of phenomena such as plasmas and particle movement. Here, the authors analyse MMS data on charge distribution, showing that there is a separation of charge on the dawn and dusk sectors of the inner magnetosphere.

      - paragraph: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion, the standard technique for generating entangled photons, is limited by low pair extraction efficiencies at near-unity fidelity.       - paragraph: Formulating a general nonequilibrium thermodynamics of quantum coherence and identifying conditions for it to affect work extraction has remained elusive.           - /url: /articles/s42005-023-01482-9
      - paragraph: "Editors Summary: Amorphous photonic structures offer a unique platform for studying unique optical transport phenomena in random media. The authors examine both experimentally and theoretically TE (in-plane) polarized near-infrared light in amorphous structures, demonstrating isotropic and asymmetric bandgaps, Anderson-like localized states at the midgap, and readily available practical waveguide structures."

          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01533-9
          - text: The pseudochiral Fermi surface of α-RuI
          - subscript: "3"
      - paragraph:
        - text: The newly-synthesised α-RuI
        - subscript: "3"
        - text: has a much-debated ground state. Here, the authors demonstrate, using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, that RuI
        - subscript: "3"
        - text: is a moderately correlated metal with an electronic band structure not having any in-plane symmetry, introducing the concept of pseudochirality to describe a similar band structure.
      - list:

        - link "Charge-neutral, GeV-scale electron-positron pair beams produced using bremsstrahlung gamma rays":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01527-7
      - paragraph: When an energetic charged particle or photon is incident on a material, matter-antimatter pairs, such as electron-positron pairs, can be created. Here, the authors successfully generate charge-neutral GeV electron-positron beams using a multi-petawatt laser via pair production from the bremsstrahlung gamma rays.
      - list:

      - heading "Enhancing polarization transfer from nitrogen-vacancy centers to external nuclear spins via dangling bond mediators" [level=3]:
        - link "Enhancing polarization transfer from nitrogen-vacancy centers to external nuclear spins via dangling bond mediators":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01536-6
      - paragraph: The use of nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is a powerful approach for quantum sensing and can enhance the sensitivity of other techniques such as nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). Here, the authors present a dynamic nuclear polarization technique, which enhances the efficiency of polarisation transfer from the NV centre at volumes suitable for NMR without being disrupted by other defects within the diamond.
      - list:

      - generic: Open Access

      - heading "Destabilization of spin-Peierls phase via a charge-spin modulated Floquet state induced by intramolecular vibrational excitation" [level=3]:
        - link "Destabilization of spin-Peierls phase via a charge-spin modulated Floquet state induced by intramolecular vibrational excitation":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01524-w
      - paragraph: Electronic state control using periodic light fields called Floquet engineering is a central topic in photophysics. The authors demonstrate an example of Floquet engineering, in which intramolecular vibrational excitation by a mid-infrared pulse in a molecular solid K-TCNQ induces a charge-spin modulated Floquet state synchronized with intramolecular vibration, destabilizing the spin Peierls phase.

        - link "Charge-4e supercurrent in a two-dimensional InAs-Al superconductor-semiconductor heterostructure":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01531-x
      - paragraph: Charge-4e transport could be useful for realizing parity-protected superconducting qubits. In this work, the authors demonstrated the controlled conversion between charge-2e dominated and charge-4e dominated supercurrent in a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) fabricated in an InAs two-dimensional electron gas proximitized by the vicinity to an epitaxial Al layer.

      - paragraph:
        - text: The reduced dimensions of 2D materials increase the strength of electron-electron correlations and hence they can be used as a platform to engineer exotic physical states such as Dirac semimetals.       - paragraph: The common probes for cold atoms systems are typically global and do not provide direct information on the local spatial structure of states, limiting the insight on disordered and quasiperiodic systems.           - subscript: "3"
          - text: )
          - subscript: "3"
      - paragraph: Materials hosting magnetic rare-earth ions sitting on a two-dimensional triangular lattices are ideal candidates to realize spin liquid states.       - paragraph: In this work, metasurface-based perfect vortex beams (MPVBs) featuring topological charges (TCs) of −32 and 16 have been successfully manufactured.         - listitem: ... Shao-Yang Huang

          - /url: /articles/s42005-023-01514-4
          - text: Order from disorder phenomena in BaCoS
          - subscript: "2"
      - paragraph: The study of frustrated magnet systems has unveiled a range of novel physical phenomena and continues to attract interest for in fields such as quantum spin liquid theory and high-temperature superconductors. Here, the authors use ab-initio calculations and a spin-wave analysis to demonstrate that an order-from-disorder phenomenon contributes to the columnar antiferromagnet ordering of BaCoS2.

          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01528-6
      - paragraph: Migdal-Eliashberg theory is a method for describing conventional superconductors. Here, the authors present an implementation that goes beyond the widely used constant density of states approximation by accommodating scattering processes beyond the Fermi surface, and they show its importance in two classes of near room temperature superhydrides.
      - list:

        - link "Observation of large spin-polarized Fermi surface of a magnetically proximitized semiconductor quantum well":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-023-01485-6
      - paragraph: Narrow-gap semiconductors with gate-controllable spin-splitting provide an ideal platform for novel spintronic and topological devices. The authors observe a large spontaneous spin-splitting energy, reaching 18 meV and widely tunable by a gate voltage, in an InAs quantum well that is magnetically proximitized by a ferromagnetic semiconductor (Ga,Fe)Sb.

      - time: 15 Jan 2024

      - heading "Generalized acoustic impedance metasurface" [level=3]:
        - link "Generalized acoustic impedance metasurface":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01529-5
      - paragraph: Impedance theory grants insight to design metasurfaces for controlling acoustic fields, but such theory imposes great limitation on boundary conditions. The authors propose a generalized acoustic impedance theory connecting arbitrarily conservative acoustic fields, and design a beam splitter as an example of power flow processing.
      - list:

        - listitem: ... Yue-Sheng Wang

      - 'heading "Chern dartboard insulator: sub-Brillouin zone topology and skyrmion multipoles" [level=3]':
        - 'link "Chern dartboard insulator: sub-Brillouin zone topology and skyrmion multipoles"':
          - /url: /articles/s42005-023-01502-8
      - paragraph: A Chern insulator has non-trivial bulk topology with a quantized Chern number defined in the Brillouin zone (BZ), yielding robust gapless edge states. The authors introduce the concept of reduced Chern number, defined in subregions of the BZ, and construct a family of Chern dartboard insulators with quantized reduced Chern numbers but trivial bulk topology, exhibiting distinct pseudospin textures.
      - list:
        - listitem: Yun-Chung Chen

      - heading "Magnetic fluid film enables almost complete drag reduction across laminar and turbulent flow regimes" [level=3]:
        - link "Magnetic fluid film enables almost complete drag reduction across laminar and turbulent flow regimes":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-023-01509-1
      - paragraph: The turbulent skin friction drag at the solid/liquid interface results in high electric energy consumption when conveying liquids through hydraulic networks, and efficient drag reduction strategies are still unavailable. The authors coat a channel with a magnetic fluid film and achieve almost complete wall drag reduction of up to 90% across laminar and turbulent flow regimes.
      - list:
        - listitem: Laura Maria Stancanelli
        - listitem: ", Eleonora Secchi"
        - listitem: "& Markus Holzner"

      - generic: Open Access

    - article:
      - heading "Multi-resolution partial differential equations preserved learning framework for spatiotemporal dynamics" [level=3]:
        - link "Multi-resolution partial differential equations preserved learning framework for spatiotemporal dynamics":
          - /url: /articles/s42005-024-01521-z
      - paragraph: Most physics-informed deep learning models alleviate the poor generalizability of pure data-driven models by minimizing residuals of the governing equations. In this work the authors propose to leverage physics priors, by embedding the discretized governing equations into the neural network architecture, which improves the generalizability and long-term prediction accuracy.
      - list:
        - listitem: Xin-Yang Liu
        - listitem: ", Min Zhu"
        - listitem: ... Jian-Xun Wang
